correctness.rationale: Direct coefficient expansion and three geometric sums reduce the infinite Wiener coefficient norm to three absolute linear forms. The exact H² coefficient Gram matrix has a verified inverse. With A>0, -B<0, C>0, the dual phase problem is the strictly concave function F(t)=At+sqrt(B²+C²-2BCt). The exact identity BC-A(B+C)=r³(1+r)³(1-2r)(1+2r)>=0 makes t=-1 the unique maximizer throughout 0<r<=1/2. The Riesz vector has aligned negative tails, so the triangle inequality is equality; r=0 follows by Cauchy–Schwarz. All quantifiers, phase degeneracies, and the endpoint r=1/2 have been checked; checker.py verifies identities with exact arithmetic.

value.rationale: The family is the canonical two-dimensional model space for a repeated Blaschke zero. This is the first nontrivial coalesced-pole rational embedding problem and fixes a sharp operator norm for a continuum of pole radii, determines all extremizers and identifies an exact phase mechanism at the natural parameter threshold 1/2. It is not merely a coefficient identity or an arbitrary finite example: it provides the missing sharp finite-degree comparison to published degree-growth estimates. The unproved larger-radius and distinct-pole regimes remain open here.
